paras: The shooting of Thomas Thompson was the shooting of a Black man, described as "colored," by an officer named Griffith at Newark, Ohio, reported in December 1881. The only report found gave the officer's circumstance, that Thompson was "attempting to escape," and said nothing of whether he survived.

According to a telegraph item, Thompson was shot at Newark, O., by "officer Griffith" while attempting to escape. The item did not give the date or place of the shooting within the town, why Thompson was in custody or being arrested, or the nature of his wound. The account that he was fleeing could only have come from the officer's side, and no other version appears in the coverage.
No report of Thompson's condition, an inquest, or any action against the officer appears in the coverage.

The Daily Evening Bulletin of Maysville, Kentucky, ran the story on December 20, 1881, as a single line in its "By Telegraph" column. It appeared among unrelated brief items, including other Ohio shootings and fires, the Guiteau trial and a death from hydrophobia, and carried no comment. The item identified Thompson by race with the word "colored," a label it gave no other person in the column.
No other paper carrying the story was found in the coverage.
